verdict.rationale: Hatchet's first-party docs describe self-hosting as running your own instance of the Hatchet Control Plane, which orchestrates workflows, schedules tasks and coordinates workers. A community user also references the self-hosted quickstart docs, and community comments note that a self-hosted stack involves Postgres plus RabbitMQ. Missing for 10: deployment specifics (Docker/Kubernetes/Helm) and open-source license terms are not evidenced, the RabbitMQ dependency adds operational burden, and there is no independent hands-on report of a successful self-hosted deployment.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: Self-hosting Hatchet means running your own instance of the Hatchet Control Plane - the central orchestration system that manages workflows, schedules tasks, and coordinates worker execution.
The actual task queue is entirely backed by Postgres, but things like streaming events between different workers are done through RabbitMQ at the moment.
